correctness.rationale: For d=m+1>=2, real symmetric signed coordinate flips T_j anticommute and square to the identity. Nonzero integer coefficients 5-4m,4,...,4 have squared sum (4m-3)^2. Thus K^2=a^2I and the edge-patterned matrix A=[[K,aI],[aI,K]] has kernel dimension 2^(d-1). Grouped by Hamming parity A=[[0,B],[B^T,0]], so rank(B)=2^(d-2) and each parity supports a 2^(d-2)-dimensional kernel. The ordinary zero-forcing kernel-injection lemma yields at least 2^(d-2) initially blue vertices on each parity. A coordinate facet forces the opposite facet, proving minimum size 2^(d-1) and equality on both parities. Sliding along any cube edge changes this fixed count, hence no slide connects two optimal sets. Dimension one is K_2 and has the stated exception. Both fully embedded standalone checkers were executed: signed identities/ranks for dimensions 2..6 and exhaustive forcing/slide enumeration through dimension four. The infinite statement relies on the complete symbolic argument, not on finite tests.

value.rationale: Local relocation of minimum zero forcing configurations is a natural robustness question in monitoring and graph reconfiguration. This complete infinite-family theorem gives a sharp threshold from the 1-cube (one legal slide) to every higher-dimensional cube (no legal slide at all), not a finite-table recomputation. It strengthens the known scalar optimum via two independent structural lower bounds and explains why an unrestricted exchange graph can be connected (as known for Q4) while its physically local token-slide graph is entirely frozen. This parity-invariant obstruction is reusable for questions about slack buffers and bipartition-preserving moves. It does not claim a general downstream theorem outside the stated family.
